record.paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
record.original_question: For abelian powers in partial words, determine the minimum alphabet size needed to construct a partial word with infinitely many holes that avoids abelian third powers, fourth powers, and fifth powers. In this setting, abelian n-freeness means that the holes can be filled with alphabet letters so that the word contains no n consecutive factors that are permutations of one another.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $\diamond \notin A$ denote a "hole" symbol that matches every letter of $A$. A partial word over $A$ is an infinite sequence $w \in (A \cup \{\diamond\})^{\mathbb{N}}$; a filling of $w$ is any word in $A^{\mathbb{N}}$ obtained from $w$ by replacing each occurrence of $\diamond$ with some letter of $A$.

Two finite words $u, v \in A^*$ are called abelian-equivalent if they have the same length and the same multiset (Parikh vector) of letters. For an integer $n \geq 2$, an abelian $n$-th power is a finite word of the form $u_1 u_2 \cdots u_n$ where $u_1, \dots, u_n$ are pairwise abelian-equivalent nonempty words. A partial word $w$ is said to avoid abelian $n$-th powers if there exists a filling of $w$ whose infinite word contains no factor that is an abelian $n$-th power.

For each $n \in \{3, 4, 5\}$, determine the minimum size $|A|$ of an alphabet $A$ for which there exists an infinite partial word over $A$ containing infinitely many holes that avoids abelian $n$-th powers.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of the minimum alphabet size needed for an infinite partial word with infinitely many holes avoiding abelian n-th powers (for n = 3, 4, 5) appears in the literature on abelian pattern avoidance in partial words as an explicit open problem. While related results have been obtained (e.g., constructions over binary alphabets avoiding abelian 6th powers, and resolved bounds for abelian squares), the exact thresholds for n = 3, 4, 5 with infinitely many holes do not appear to have been determined in subsequent work.

status_evidence.title: Abelian pattern avoidance in partial words
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates smallest alphabet size needed to construct an infinite partial word with finitely or infinitely many holes that avoids abelian p-th powers.
status_evidence.claim: The minimum alphabet sizes for avoiding abelian 3rd, 4th and 5th powers with infinitely many holes are posed as questions, not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Avoiding Abelian Powers in Partial Words
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of infinite binary partial words with infinitely many holes avoiding abelian 6th powers are given.
status_evidence.claim: Only the case of 6th powers (and higher) over binary alphabets has been settled with infinitely many holes; the 3rd, 4th, 5th cases remain open.
